question.text: On March 30, 1981, this man shot Ronald Reagan in an attempt to impress Jodie Foster, but failed to kill him.
question.clue: Following this man's most notable action, his victim allegedly joked "I hope you're all Republicans" to his doctors.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Republican Presidential hopefuls in the 2012 primary season.
swap.text: After only being allowed to compete in a small number of debates, this former New Mexico governor ran for president with the backing of the Libertarian Party.
swap.clue: This politician was referred to as "Puff Daddy" by Clinton drug czar Barry McCaffrey for his endorsement of marijuana legalization.

question.text: During the Katrina benefit concert, this man went off-script to controversially state "George Bush doesn't care about black people."

swap.text: The first Jewish woman to serve on the Supreme Court, she served for 13 years on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit before being nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993.
swap.clue: This co-founder of the ACLU's Women's Rights Project struck down VMI's male-only admission policy as part of her longtime advocacy for women's rights.

question.leadin: This phrase was popularized by Alyssa Milano, who took inspiration from civil rights activist Tarana Burke.
question.text: Name this two-word hashtag that has been used to share stories and spread awareness of sexual harassment. It gained popularity after accusations directed at film executive Harvey Weinstein.
question.clue: This movement with a namesake hashtag in which women are admitting to having experienced sexual harassment or assault, especially in the workplace. It is related to the Time's Up movement.

swap.leadin: Name these sieges that took place around the world.
swap.text: In 1993, the FBI besieged the Mount Carmel Center in Waco, Texas after gunfire from this group was directed at ATF agents. The siege resulted in the death of this sect's leader, David Koresh.

question.leadin: Name these things related to the 2010 earthquake in Haiti.
question.text: This evangelist described the earthquake as the result of Haitians' "pact to the Devil" in order to liberate them from French colonists.

swap.text: This former Congresswoman from the Eighth District of Arizona started the Americans for Responsible Solutions PAC [pack] to advocate against gun violence after she was shot in the head at a Safeway near Tucson in 2011.
swap.clue: She received a standing ovation from Congress when she appeared to cast a vote in August 2011.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Watergate scandal.
question.text: This man, the solicitor general, ended up carrying out the firing of Cox when Richardson and William Ruckelshaus refused. His later failed nomination to the Supreme Court transformed his name into a verb denoting the derailing of congressional confirmation.
question.clue: This man, who complied in firing Archibald Cox during the Saturday Night Massacre, was the focus of a committee hearing, led by Joe Biden, that decided not to replace Lewis Powell with this man.

swap.leadin: Name these things from America's Cuba policy.
swap.text: This 1996 act codified the longstanding embargo on Cuba and allows U.S. citizens to sue companies which do business on Cuban properties that were nationalized from Americans.

question.leadin: The evil of this figure radiates clearly from his bald pate and savagely grinning countenance, which resemble those of fictional evildoers Lex Luthor and Voldemort.
question.text: Who is this governor-elect of Florida, to that state's eternal shame?
question.clue: In 2010, Jeromy helped elect this tea-party aligned conservative as governor of Florida. This bald businessman narrowly defeated Democrat Alex Sink in the general election.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people's reactions to the 2011 earthquake in Japan.
swap.text: This governor of Mississippi, considered a potential Republican presidential candidate in 2012, saw his press secretary, Dan Turner, resign after a Turner e-mail cracked that the song "(Sittin' on) the Dock of the Bay" was not popular in Japan right now.
swap.clue: This man's former lobbying firm, which is named for himself, Griffith and Rogers, may have engaged in corporate espionage on behalf of Alfa Bank.

question.text: "Read my lips" was described as "the most famous broken promise in the history of American politics" by this Clinton campaign strategist, who also coined the phrase "It's the economy, stupid."

swap.leadin: Identify these people whose seats were contested in the 2012 elections.
swap.text: This former Representative from Texas, nicknamed "Dr. No," retired from the House to run for president in 2012, but failed to win the Republican nomination.
swap.clue: This representative and MD from Texas once ran as a libertarian about 20 years ago. He's notable for opposing the PATRIOT act and advocating a non-interventionist foreign policy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Republican Revolution of 1994.
question.text: This Georgia representative replaced Bob Michel as leader of the Republicans in the House, ascending to the office of Speaker in 1994. About a year later, his standoff with Clinton led to a government shutdown.

swap.leadin: Name some winners of 2014 midterm elections.
swap.text: This Republican Kansas governor was re-elected despite more than a hundred Republicans endorsing his Democratic opponent in response to this man's extensive, revenue-negative tax cuts.
swap.clue: This senator from Kansas is a total redneck who advocates complete banning of abortion and a flat tax, and wants to "renew the family".

question.text: The more moderate New York hipster Abbie Hoffman wrote this work in 1970, which refers to America as the "Pig Izak Haber claimed that much of it was Empire" and is divided into the sections "Survive!", "Fight!", and "Liberate!"plagiarized.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about US gubernatorial elections in 2013.
swap.text: In New Jersey, this female state senator is the most likely Democratic nominee to run against Republican Chris Christie.

question.leadin: Answer questions about the doomed Equal Rights Amendment.
question.text: This founder of the Eagle Forum campaigned to "Stop the Equal Rights Amendment" as it would eliminate nebulous "privileges" and force women into unisex bathrooms. Five states rescinded their ratifications after her anti-ERA campaign began. Her son Andrew runs the website Conservapedia.
question.clue: This activist founded the Eagle Forum which grew out of a movement named STOP or "Stop Taking Our Privileges."

swap.text: This political advocacy group split off from Citizens for a Sound Economy in 2004. Obama named it as one of the "shadowy groups with harmless sounding names," and its agents were criticized for plastering fake eviction notices on Detroit homes in June of 2011.
